bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Board 12th Exam Date 2027 Soon: BSEB Inter Time Table PDF, Exam Form Closes October 31
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Board 12th Exam Date 2027: Time Table Release Date Last cycle, BSEB’s official X handle posted the programme for the Intermediate Annual Examination 2026 on December 22, 2025 . That single notice covered the Science, Arts, Commerce and Vocational streams. Going by that, the BSEB Inter Time Table 2027 is expected by December 2026. Event Date Status Exam form, fourth window (late fee) October 16 to 31, 2026 Open Exam fee payment last date October 30, 2026 Official Exam form last date October 31, 2026 Official Bihar Board 12th Date Sheet 2027 By December 2026 Expected Bihar Board 12th Exam Date 2027 (theory) In the date sheet PDF Releasing soon Bihar Board 12th Exam Form 2027 Last Date and Fee The first window ran from August 25 to September 16, 2026, under BSEB notice P.R. 193/2026 . The current window is open with a late fee; the notice lists the base fees below. Category Total fee Regular, private and ex-regular (first-time applicants) Rs 1,430 Improvement and qualifying Rs 1,770 Vocational, regular Rs 1,830 Vocational, improvement Rs 2,170 Vocational, ex-regular failed Rs 1,490 Ex-regular failed (Arts, Science, Commerce) Rs 1,090 Compartmental Rs 960 Each total includes a Rs 30 online fee kept by the school. Regular SC, ST and EBC students are exempt from the Rs 260 examination fee. Payment is accepted through Indian Bank e-challan, debit or credit card, net banking, or RTGS/NEFT. Students do not fill the form online themselves. Each student fills the printed form in two copies and gives both to the school head, who returns one signed and stamped copy and submits the form online with the student’s Unique ID. A form will not go through if the signed declaration on the dummy registration card was never uploaded. Regular, private and qualifying candidates who miss the sent-up exam or are not sent up will not get an admit card. The BSEB helpline is 0612-2230039. How to Download Bihar Board 12th Exam Date 2027 PDF Go to biharboardonline.bihar.gov.in . Open the Intermediate Annual Examination 2027 programme notice once it is live. Download the PDF and match each subject code with the codes on your registration certificate. Note your shift for every paper. Bihar Board 12th Exam Date 2027: Expected Timeline Particulars 2026 cycle (Official) 2027 cycle (Expected) Date sheet release November 29, 2025 Late November to early December 2026 Theory exams February 2 to 13, 2026 First half of February 2027 Until the board publishes the programme PDF, any Bihar Board 12th Exam Date 2027 in circulation is an estimate.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar polls: Saran teachers' constituency leads with 13.56% turnout in first two hours
bihar_raw_news.content: Representative image File Photo Bihar Bihar polls: Saran teachers’ constituency leads with 13.56% turnout in first two hours As many as 5.32 lakh voters were eligible to decide the fate of 150 candidates contesting the eight seats. TNIE online desk Updated: 23rd Oct, 2026 at 11:43 AM Polling for the biennial elections to eight Bihar Legislative Council seats recorded brisk turnout in the first two hours on Friday, with the Saran Teachers’ constituency registering the highest polling percentage at 13.56%, followed by Patna Teachers’ at 12.88%. As many as 5.32 lakh voters were eligible to decide the fate of 150 candidates contesting the eight seats. According to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Darbhanga recorded the highest turnout among the Graduates’ constituencies at 8%, followed by Patna at 5.5%, Kosi at 5.14% and Tirhut at 4.81%. Among the Teachers’ constituencies, Saran recorded the highest turnout, followed by Patna. Darbhanga registered 12%, while Tirhut recorded 5.88%. The average turnout stood at 5.86% across the Graduates’ constituencies and 11.08% across the Teachers’ constituencies. Polling began at 8 am and is scheduled to continue until 4 pm. The combined electorate comprises 5,32,847 voters, including 1,46,611 women and 37 third-gender voters, across 933 polling stations. Counting will take place on 27 October. “Polling has so far been peaceful,” an official said. The contest in the Patna Graduates’ constituency has attracted particular attention following a rift within the Janata Dal (United), with Mokama MLA Anant Singh backing Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh against his own party’s nominee, Neeraj Kumar. Kumar, a former minister and close aide of former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, is seeking a fourth consecutive term from the constituency. Anant Singh has extended his support to Anuj Singh, alleging that Neeraj Kumar worked against him during last year’s Assembly elections. “People are the real masters. It is for them to decide the fate of candidates. I am confident that Anuj Singh will win the election with a massive mandate,” Singh told reporters. Also read: PK, independent candidates make Bihar poll fray intense Add as a preferred source on Google Commenting on Nitish Kumar’s brief meeting with Neeraj Kumar on Thursday, Singh said the JD(U) chief “goes wherever they take him”. Singh and Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor have repeatedly claimed that Neeraj Kumar does not enjoy the support of the party chief. Meanwhile, JD(U) leader Shyam Rajak, whose party is a key constituent of the ruling alliance, said polling was proceeding smoothly and claimed that the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) was enjoying a wave of support. Besides Patna Graduates, polling is being held in Darbhanga Graduates, Tirhut Graduates, Kosi Graduates, Patna Teachers, Darbhanga Teachers, Tirhut Teachers and Saran Teachers. national_raw_news.title: India and Uzbekistan agree to strengthen cooperation against terrorism and regional security threats
national_raw_news.content: India and Uzbekistan today agreed to cooperate in addressing the threats and challenges to national and regional security, and further strengthen the framework of the India-Uzbekistan Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism. The tenth meeting of India-Uzbekistan Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism was held in New Delhi. The two sides discussed the threats posed by terrorist groups globally and in their respective regions. Both sides exchanged views on current and emerging challenges to counter-terrorism. These include countering extremism and radicalization, combating financing of terrorism, preventing use of technology for terrorist purposes, and the nexus between transnational organized crime and terrorism. External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that the two sides also deliberated on the measures to strengthen bilateral cooperation in the sphere of counter terrorism through information sharing, capacity building and sharing of best practices. They discussed the prospects of developing cooperation in the fight against terrorism between the relevant agencies of India and Uzbekistan. Both sides reaffirmed commitment to strengthen cooperation in multilateral fora including the UN, SCO-RATS and EAG. The meeting was co-chaired by Additional Secretary (Counter Terrorism), Ministry of External Affairs, Dr. Suhel Ajaz Khan and Head of the Department for Cooperation with South Asian, Near, Middle Eastern and African Countries under Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pirimkulov Gulomjon Shodmonkulovich.

national_raw_news.title: Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit
national_raw_news.content: Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit ANI | Updated: Oct 22, 2026 19:45 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, on Thursday organised the fourth virtual conference with States and Union Territories as part of a series of thematic consultations being held in follow-up to the Departmental Summit on Water 2026 held on September 1 and 2. The conference focused on strengthening convergence between Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and the 16th Finance Commission to advance source sustainability, water security and Gram Panchayat-led planning for sustainable rural drinking water service delivery. The virtual conference brought together senior officials from State PHEDs/Rural Water Supply Departments, Panchayati Raj Departments and representatives from the Ministries of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India and National Informatics Centre. State rural water supply departments, including Karnataka, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh, shared best practices and field experiences on leveraging Finance Commission grants for strengthening rural water supply systems, improving O&M arrangements, enhancing community participation and strengthening local governance mechanisms. Addressing the conference, Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, stated that with the extension of JJM 2.0, the focus now shifts from infrastructure creation to ensuring functionality, sustainability and quality service delivery. He emphasised that the true measure of success lies not merely in asset creation but in ensuring that rural households continue to receive reliable and safe drinking water through well-maintained and financially sustainable systems. Meena underlined the pivotal role of Gram Panchayats in rural water governance and noted that the 73rd Constitutional Amendment places drinking water and sanitation among the key responsibilities of local self-governments. He stressed that Gram Panchayats must take leadership in preparing comprehensive annual O&M plans, mobilising local resources, managing service delivery and ensuring accountability for water supply infrastructure created under JJM and other programmes. Referring to the 16th Finance Commission framework, he highlighted that tied grants provide a significant opportunity to strengthen the sustainability of drinking water and sanitation services at the grassroots level. He noted that of the total Rural Local Body (RLB) grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, a substantial share has been earmarked for water and sanitation-related activities. He emphasised that these grants should be utilised primarily for operation and maintenance, source sustainability, water quality management, service delivery improvements and strengthening local institutional capacity rather than creation of new infrastructure where existing assets require maintenance and support. The Secretary focused on three key pillars of sustainable financing for rural water supply systems such as effective utilisation of Finance Commission grants, ii. convergence with other available programmes, and iii. schemes, and progressive strengthening of user-charge collection mechanisms. national_raw_news.title: Comprehensive Capacity Building recommendations by Committee in MoSPI
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Towards Future-Ready Data Leaders: Comprehensive Capacity Building recommendations by Committee in MoSPI Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 11:03PM by PIB Delhi The chairman of the Committee for Reforming Capacity Building of the Indian Statistical Service (ISS), Sh. P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) submitted the Committee's report to Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI. This marks an important milestone toward strengthening the capacity-building framework for ISS officers. The Committee comprised senior MoSPI officers, knowledge partners, and industry experts. The Committee reviewed existing ISS training programmes, identified emerging capacity building requirements, and recommended future-oriented training aligned with the Competency Based Capacity Building (CBCB) framework of Mission Karmayogi . The framework reflects the evolving role of ISS officers in data governance, advanced analytics, emerging technologies, and evidence-based policymaking, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. The report has been prepared through a consultative and evidence-based approach, drawing on the Statistical Training Needs Assessment, existing ISS training programmes, Mission Karmayogi frameworks, international best practices, Committee deliberations, and stakeholder consultations. The Report presents a future oriented capacity building roadmap comprising three interconnected components. The System of Today , which reviews the existing ISS training ecosystem, capability area practices, and institutional arrangements at National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) . The System of Tomorrow , which establishes a role linked, competency based capacity-building framework covering seven priority capability pillars; and Strategic Recommendations giving actionable measures to transition from current to the envisioned future system to strengthening ISS training, develop future ready competencies, and enhance NSSTA's institutional capacity. The report outlines an integrated framework comprising the ISS training ecosystem, capability pillars, and institutional architecture. It defines role expectations and assesses the competencies required for each role across functional, domain, and behavioral domains. The framework is to be anchored in the National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) , with an emphasis on strengthening human resources, training delivery, and governance to effectively implement training reforms. Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, complimented the Committee and the NSSTA team for their efforts and comprehensive, forward-looking recommendations. He reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening NSSTA as a pivotal training anchor for Indian Statistical Systems.
